messages:
mina: quick check-in — I ran a few microbenchmarks on the paged-attn path with the new adaptive slab allocator for the block-table. results are noisy but there's a consistent throughput valley around seq_len=1024 for batched small prompts. attaching the perf snip below

jonathan: curious — is this the allocator that splits hot vs cold slab pools?

mina: yeah, split into hot (<=4k entries) and cold (>4k). adaptive freelist migrates blocks after N accesses. trying to reduce internal fragmentation and large memcpy churn.

sam: can you paste the perf lines?

mina: sure — from the profiler (nvprof style):
```
Kernel: flash_attn_v2_fused  Time: 1.8ms  SMs: 84%  WarpStalls: 12%
Kernel: paged_kv_pagewalk   Time: 0.6ms  SMs: 22%  MemBW: 48%
KV alloc/free ratio: 1.03
Block-table hits: 87% -> 72% at seq_len=1024
Page faults (soft): +2100/s when pack size > 8
```

rachel: that block-table hit drop is suspicious. did the migration policy trigger more evictions at that size?

mina: yes looks like the migrator starts moving entries out of hot slabs once the hot pool is ~78% full. moving creates transient CPU work and pagewalk churn.

jonathan: two quick ideas: lower the migration threshold to 68% for the experiment, and opportunistically prefetch adjacent blocks for hot keys. prefetch might smooth mem bandwidth.

sam: prefetch might also increase contention for the slab lock. how heavy is our global lock right now?

mina: we use per-shard locks (256 shards). contention is low except during compaction bursts. compaction = global-ish serial phase.

rachel: could the batching heuristics be interacting? when throughput dips we switch kernel variants (flashattn-v2 -> fused-batched) which has different memory access patterns. if the runtime switches kernels mid-batch are we invalidating the KV layout assumptions?

mina: good point — we do kernel selection per-request group based on median seq_len and predicted latency. when a batch contains mixed seq_lens we pick the lower-latency kernel and then pagewalks spike.

sam: maybe add a safeguard: if >20% of batch memory accesses hit cold pages, prefer memory-friendly kernel even if nominal latency is higher.

jonathan: agree. also would like to see trace of a full request: include kernel switch markers, slab migrations, and per-token wait times. can we get a lightweight tracer?

mina: i pushed a short tracer to the perf branch — run with `REDWOOD_TRACER=kv-mig,ker-switch:1`  will log events to stdout. example line: `T 2065432107 mina: ker-switch flash->fused batch=12 seqs=[32,64,1024...] mig:start shard=7 freed=128`

rachel: can you run the experiment with lowered migrate threshold + the tracer turned on and post a small excerpt?

mina: running now on a dedicated test run (dedicated-serve-3). will post results in ~10m.

ci-bot: deploy started by mina on dedicated-serve-3 (run id: d3-2065432100). tests: paged-kv-smoke, flashattn-regress.

mina: results (short): lowering threshold -> block-table hit improves to 81% at seq_len=1024; pagewalks drop ~45%; overall token throughput +6% for mixed batches. but single long seq throughput drops ~4%.

sam: sounds like a win for mixed workloads. can we make threshold dynamic per-model? some workloads have stable long sequences, others are chatty short ones.

jonathan: idea: per-model policy that observes recent seq_len distribution (exponential window) and sets migrate threshold and kernel hint accordingly. cheap to compute.

mina: we prototyped per-model in the branch. downside: policy churn when distribution oscillates — need hysteresis. adding a 3-window majority rule seems to work.

rachel: what about KV cache eviction order? currently LRU on per-shard slabs? could we try segmented-LRU where hot segment is protected for a TTL based on access frequency?

mina: segmented-LRU is similar to current hot/cold but we can back it with rate-limiting for migration to prevent compaction storms. planning an A/B.

jonathan: small perf regression note: i saw an old CI run where fused kernel had a 2% latency tail increase after a memory allocator tweak — keep an eye on p95 and p99 in the dashboard.

mina: noted. i'll run the per-model policy + segmented-LRU A/B and collect p50/p95/p99 plus kernel-switch traces. posting results later today.

rachel: thanks — this is great. if A/B looks good we should gate it behind an opt-in rollout and add the fallback policy: if p95 regresses by >5% revert.

mina: agreed. will add rollout with canary=5% -> 20% -> 100% and automatic rollback on regressions.

sam: tiny follow-up: update the docs in eng-runtime/README about the new tracer flags so SRE can use them during incidents.

mina: will do.

jonathan: bravo for the tracer — super helpful. :clap:

mina: thanks all. will upload the trace excerpt and the branch link when done.
